policies.title: United States ordinary passport: North Macedonia short visitor stay
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance establishes a visa-free ordinary U.S.-passport tourist or business visit to North Macedonia for less than 90 days in six months.
conditions: The visa-free scope is tourism or business for less than 90 days within a six-month period.
Work, study, longer stays, passport validity, medical insurance, registration, admission, and dual-nationality rules remain outside this classification.

policies.title: United States ordinary passport: Côte d’Ivoire preapproved arrival visa
policies.summary: A U.S.-passport visitor must request approval online before arrival, while Côte d’Ivoire's current official procedure prints and issues the visa after airport biometrics.
conditions: Complete the online request and obtain approval before travel; the visa itself is printed and issued after biometric enrolment at Abidjan airport.
The ordinary visitor must also satisfy passport, yellow-fever, carrier, entry-point, and final-admission conditions.

policies.title: United States ordinary passport: specified arrival-issued visitor visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance expressly provides arrival-issued visa routes for ordinary U.S. passports in Guinea-Bissau and Jordan.
conditions: GW: a visa is required and may be obtained on arrival; advance embassy application is also available.

JO: visas are issued on arrival at Queen Alia International Airport and most international land crossings, but not at King Hussein (Allenby Bridge); stay, fee, registration, Jordan Pass, e-application, purpose, document, and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: United States ordinary passport: expressly pre-travel visitor visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance expressly requires an ordinary U.S.-passport visitor to obtain a visa before travel to Liberia or Niger.
conditions: LR: all tourist visits require an advance visa; a traveler without one may be deported immediately.
NE: an advance visa is required; destination-specific passport, yellow-fever, security, carrier, entry-point, and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: United States ordinary passport: Sierra Leone pre-travel visitor visa
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance requires an ordinary U.S.-passport visitor to obtain a Sierra Leone visa before travel.
conditions: The visa is required regardless of the length of stay and must be applied for before travel.
The separately paid airport-security fee is not a visa or an arrival-issuance route.

policies.title: United States ordinary passport: Paraguay short visitor stay
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance establishes visa-free ordinary U.S.-passport tourism or business access to Paraguay for up to 90 days.
conditions: The scope is private U.S. citizens visiting for tourism or business for up to 90 days.
Passport validity, child-travel, departure-tax, special-document, and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Mali suspends entry for United States nationals
policies.summary: Mali's Foreign Ministry suspends entry to Mali for United States nationals under a reciprocal measure, subject to its express valid-visa, residence, category, and national-interest exceptions.
conditions: The signed 30 December 2025 communiqué applies the measure to U.S. nationals with immediate effect; the signed 2 January 2026 communiqué sets out its implementation.
United States nationals permanently resident in Mali and United States nationals holding a currently valid Malian visa are excepted from the entry suspension.
The stated exceptions also include certain categories of United States nationals, including athletes, diplomats, and persons whose entry serves the interests of the Republic of Mali.
Mali states that the measure will be evaluated and that any adjustment will be communicated through the usual channels.

conflicts.explanation: Online approval is required before travel, but SNEDAI's current officially recognised procedure prints and issues the visa only after biometric enrolment at Abidjan airport.

Burkina Faso's signed government communiqué applies reciprocal measures in visa matters to U.S. nationals, and current State guidance reports a visa suspension from 30 December 2025. Neither source says that a U.S.-passport holder with a valid existing Burkina Faso visa is barred from entry, so entry_restricted is not established.

conflicts.officialStatus: unavailable (not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens)
conflicts.explanation: The current State Department page says Chad is not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens and that visas are not available on arrival. The fallback’s ordinary advance-visa classification therefore does not represent current ordinary issuance.

Mali's signed Foreign Ministry implementation communiqué expressly suspends entry of U.S. nationals, with exceptions for valid visas, permanent residents, certain categories, and national-interest entrants. That current entry restriction supersedes the fallback advance-visa classification.

The current State Department page says a visa is required regardless of stay length and must be applied for before travel. Its separately described airport-security fee is not a visa or arrival-issuance route.
The current State Department page says private U.S. citizens do not need a visa for tourism or business stays up to 90 days; it does not describe an arrival-visa requirement.

unresolved.reason: The current State Department page requires a valid Afghan visa for U.S. citizens but does not establish an ordinary visitor issuance channel or timing. It also warns that immigration officials may reject visas issued by certain Afghan missions. No e-visa, advance-consular, or arrival-issuance classification is inferred.

The current State Department page says a tourist visa is required, but does not establish its ordinary visitor issuance timing. In addition, a normal U.S. passport is not valid for travel to or through North Korea without a special validation. No ordinary advance-visa or arrival-issuance classification is inferred.

The current State Department page says a tourist visa is required except for Kish Island, but does not establish an ordinary visitor issuance channel or timing for a U.S. passport. The Kish exception and significant U.S.-national detention risks prevent inferring a nationwide advance-visa, e-visa, or arrival-visa rule.

Current State Department guidance is route- and territory-specific: ETA-IL is required to enter Israel for an ordinary U.S. visitor to the West Bank, while Gaza is separately subject to current access and security restrictions. It does not establish one ordinary visitor ETA, visa, eVisa, visa-free, or arrival-visa relationship for the exact PS destination scope; no complement is inferred.
